question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**would**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses routine actions that happened whenever the car stopped.
 
• In this context, "would" is used to express habitual actions in the past.
 
• "**Would**" fits well as it denotes actions that happened regularly or usually in the past.
 
• Other options ("**can**", "**should**", "**could**") do not fit the context of describing routine or habitual actions that happened in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *He knew everyone on the island. Whenever his car stopped, half a dozen voices **would **__shout out his name. Policemen, agricultural labourers of low social status and priests waved and smiled ____ 2 ____ he passed; everyone greeted him as a brother. They respected his honesty, and belligerence, and above all, they adored his typically Greek scorn and fearlessness when dealing with any _____ 3 ____ of Governmental red tape. On arrival, two of our cases containing linen and other things had been ______ 4 ____ by the Customs on the curious ground that they were merchandise. So, when we moved out to the villa and the problem of bed linen arose, Mother told Spiro ______ 5 _____ our cases in the Customs and asked for his advice.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Can (सकना): Not suitable as it talks about the capability or possibility rather than routine actions.
 
• Should (चाहिए): Implies something is expected or recommended, but not habitual actions.
 
• Could (सकता था): Indicates possibility in the past under certain conditions, not habitual actions.
